text:
marta: Quick ask — two engineers on my team have overlapping parental leaves (July mid -> Aug). Can people-ops confirm the minimal paperwork and a fast coverage playbook? Need to decide contractor vs internal rotation by Friday.

people-ops: Minimal paperwork: employees submit Parental Leave Request form, confirm FMLA/state eligibility, and upload birth/adoption docs within 30 days. For company pay-topup enrollments, payroll cutoff is the 15th of the month for the pay period covering the first paid week. Form: https://hr.redwood.example/forms/parental-leave

payroll: If you expect paid top-up, submit estimated dates + a recent paystub to payroll@redwood.example. We will model combined payments to avoid duplication with state benefits. Missing the payroll cutoff delays first top-up payment; retro pay is possible but slower.

hiring-ops-bot: Fast contractor flow: manager headcount note + 3 bullet role summary + hourly cap = ticket. Fast-track: 8-12 business days if flagged urgent-temp.

devon: For coverage I prefer internal rotation for the first 4 weeks and a short-term contractor for sustained oncall. How should we structure runbooks?

people-ops: Runbook minimal: 1) One-paragraph deploy steps, 2) Top 5 alerts + triage steps, 3) Escalation contacts, 4) One-week failover checklist, 5) Two 5-10min Looms. Pairing: two 1-hr shadow sessions in final 10 days pre-leave.

benefits: Health coverage remains active during paid company leave. If employee goes unpaid later, payroll triggers COBRA. FSAs need plan-admin review for mid-year changes. Contact benefits@redwood.example for edge cases.

marta: Great — I'll ask both to file the form today and post tentative dates here. Please open a hiring ops ticket in case we go contractor; I'll add hourly cap once I know dates. Thanks everyone.
